import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/test_3.csv"
]

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# - All source tables share the same schema.
# - Target table has only one column: 'attributes' (string).
# - Source tables have an 'attributes' column but many values are NaN.
# - We want to produce a single column 'attributes' containing all non-null attribute values from all sources.
# - Since the target examples show distinct attribute strings, we will extract all non-null 'attributes' values from all sources,
#   concatenate them, drop duplicates and NaNs, and reset index.
# - This approach uses UNION of the 'attributes' column from all sources.

# Extract 'attributes' column from each source, drop NaNs
attr0 = df0['attributes'].dropna()
attr1 = df1['attributes'].dropna()
attr2 = df2['attributes'].dropna()
attr3 = df3['attributes'].dropna()

# Concatenate all attributes series
all_attributes = pd.concat([attr0, attr1, attr2, attr3], ignore_index=True)

# Drop duplicates and reset index
all_attributes = all_attributes.drop_duplicates().reset_index(drop=True)

# Create the target DataFrame with the required schema
target_df = pd.DataFrame({'attributes': all_attributes})

# Save the result to the specified path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_91/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
